meta.title: PLOT TWIST!
meta.description: You create the characters. They create the chaos. A pixel-art storytelling sandbox for original characters.

language.label: Language
language.note: Only the interface changes. Your characters and stories stay in the language you wrote them in.

worlds.heading: Where does it all go wrong?
worlds.intro: Pick the world your characters live in. You can change it later.

western-fantasy.name: Western Fantasy
western-fantasy.blurb: Mossy villages, crooked castles and prophecies nobody reads to the end.

modern.name: Modern
modern.blurb: Cafés, late trains and group chats where secrets hide in plain sight.

ancient-china.name: Ancient China
ancient-china.blurb: Courtyards, roadside inns and wandering swordsmen with debts of honor.

otherworld.name: Otherworld
otherworld.blurb: Floating islands, glowing plants and rules of physics that change their minds.

studio.heading: Assemble your cast
studio.introWorld: Your story takes place in {world}. Everything saves automatically in this browser.
studio.intro: Everything saves automatically in this browser.
studio.emptyBody: Create your first original character. Who are they, and what are they hiding?
studio.deleteBody: {name} will be gone for good. This can't be undone.

portrait.title: Portrait
portrait.note: Placeholder portraits. Your own art, a pixel editor or AI portraits can plug into this frame later.

studio.methodsNote: Describe your character in words, with sliders, or both. The two are saved separately and sliders never rewrite what you wrote.

personality.label: Personality
personality.placeholder: Curious, impatient, kind in a loud way...

background.label: Background
background.placeholder: Where do they come from? What happened?

goals.label: Goals
goals.placeholder: What do they want more than anything?

fears.label: Fears
fears.placeholder: What would they never admit to being scared of?

habits.label: Habits & preferences
habits.placeholder: Little things they do without thinking. Favorite foods, pet peeves...

rules.label: Character rules & boundaries
rules.placeholder: Things this character would NEVER do, or topics the story should avoid.

identity.label: Identity
identity.placeholder: Role, job, title, species... e.g. apprentice cartographer

values.label: Values & beliefs
values.placeholder: What do they believe is right? What won't they compromise on?

speakingStyle.label: Speaking style
speakingStyle.placeholder: Short sentences? Big words? A catchphrase? Never swears?

canon.label: Must stay consistent
canon.placeholder: Key facts the story must never contradict. One per line.

lock.hint: Locked details are canon. The AI must keep them exactly as written.

builder.heading: Set the scene
builder.intro: Describe where your story begins and pick a type of place. The preview uses placeholder art for now.
builder.describePlaceholder: A cramped bookshop above a noodle stand. It always smells like rain, and the back door is locked from the inside...
builder.describeHint: Saved automatically. Later, this text will drive AI map generation.
builder.quoteEmpty: No description yet. Your words will appear here.

play.noWorldBody: Every story needs somewhere to happen. Pick a world first.
play.demoNotice: You haven't created anyone yet, so a demo cast is standing in.
play.selectInScene: Select a character in the scene.
play.keyboardHint: Keys: ← → choose · Z talk · X observe · C wait · V twist · L log · Esc pause

log.empty: Nothing has happened yet. Talk to someone.

play.aiFallback: AI writing didn't work ({reason}), so a built-in line was used.

sidebar.noBonds: No bonds yet. Events between characters build them.

scene.intro: The {place} is quiet. Too quiet. Pick someone and see what happens.
scene.silent: ...  (They have nothing to say yet. Give them goals or fears in the Character Studio.)
scene.observeEmpty: You look at {name}. They're still a sketch.
wait: Time passes in the {place}. Nobody admits they're waiting for something.
A quiet moment in the {place}. {name} glances your way.
Somewhere in the {place}, something creaks. Everyone pretends not to notice.

a.name: Juniper
a.appearance: They keep tucking a pencil behind their ear and forgetting it's there.
a.personality: Curious, impatient, kind in a loud way.
a.goals: Find out who left the letter on my doorstep.
a.fears: That the letter was meant for someone else.
a.relationships: Owes Rook a favor. Won't say what for.

b.name: Rook
b.appearance: Long coat, tired eyes, very clean boots.
b.personality: Dry humor, says less than they know.
b.habits: Rook taps the table twice before answering any question.
b.goals: Keep everyone out of trouble. Mostly Juniper.
b.fears: Being needed and not showing up.

load.heading: Save file
load.intro: Your game is saved in this browser automatically.
load.emptyBody: Start a new game to create your first save.

settings.title: Settings
settings.crtDesc: Old-TV lines over the whole screen.
settings.motionDesc: Turns off page transitions and bouncing.
settings.offlineReady: Everything except the AI features works offline after your first visit. Saves live in this browser.
settings.offlineFuture: AI analysis, AI dialogue and pixel generation need an internet connection and API keys on the server.
settings.dangerDesc: Deletes your world, characters and story log from this browser.
settings.eventFrequencyDesc: How often waiting turns into a plot twist.
settings.aiStoryDesc: Let the AI write dialogue when it's set up. Off means built-in lines only.

sliders.title: Personality sliders
sliders.intro: Each slider is a tendency, not a rule. Leave any of them unset and the game reads your written profile instead.

conflicts.title: Review differences
conflicts.intro: Your written profile and the sliders seem to disagree here. Both can be true at once, so you decide. Nothing changes until you pick.
conflicts.item: You wrote “{words}”, but the {trait} slider is at {value} ({lean}).
conflicts.keepBothHint: It's nuance. The AI will treat it as a situational difference.
conflicts.none: No differences between your text and the sliders.

memories.confide: the time {with} opened up to them
memories.temptation: the day they almost broke a rule
memories.fearTrigger: the moment their fear came close

analysis.title: Behavior analysis
analysis.intro: The analysis reads your written profile, sliders, relationships, rules, memories and current mood, and turns them into a behavioral profile. You review it before it affects the story.
analysis.unavailableHint: Add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to .env.local and restart the app. The built-in analysis works offline in the meantime.
analysis.needInput: Write something in the profile or set a slider first.
analysis.stale: You've edited this character since this analysis. Run it again to include the changes.
analysis.notUsedYet: Until you approve an analysis, play uses your sliders and written profile directly.

local.summaryNeutral: {name} is balanced on every slider so far, so the written profile carries the most weight.

decision.mixed: Careful with big choices, quick with small ones.

social.out: Seeks people out and fills silences.
social.in: Keeps a small circle and needs time alone.
social.mixed: Comfortable in a group, but picks their moments.

triggers.act: When there's a chance to do something
triggers.cooperate: When a problem is too big for one person

variations.confront: With people they trust, they argue more gently.
variations.deflect: If it truly matters, they face it eventually.
variations.withdraw: Around someone they trust, they open up instead.
variations.comfort: When they're hurting themselves, they may need comfort back.
variations.joke: In a real crisis the jokes stop.
variations.investigate: With close friends they ask instead of assuming.
variations.act: When someone else is at stake, they slow down.
variations.cooperate: If trust breaks, they go it alone.

local.conflictNote: Your text and this slider point different ways. Both can be true; review it on the Personality tab.

errors.invalid_output: the AI's answer didn't pass validation
errors.rate_limited: too many requests, try again in a moment
errors.failed: the AI service had a problem
errors.too_large: the image is larger than 8 MB
errors.bad_type: only PNG, JPG or WebP images work

sprite.title: Pixel character
sprite.intro: Upload a picture of your character and turn it into a standing sprite (32×32) and portrait (96×96) in the game's pixel style.
sprite.standingOnly: Standing pose only. Walking animations aren't part of this version.
sprite.fileHint: PNG, JPG or WebP · up to 8 MB
sprite.referenceNote: Shown only here and never saved. Your original file is not changed.
sprite.permission: I made this image or have permission to use it.
sprite.generatingHint: This can take up to a minute.
sprite.unavailableHint: Add OPENAI_API_KEY to .env.local and restart the app to turn it on. You can still use the quick conversion below.
sprite.convertHint: Shrinks your picture straight into sprite pixels. Works best on drawings with a plain background.
sprite.saved: Saved to {name} and your sprite library.
sprite.libraryEmpty: Sprites you save appear here, and any character can reuse them.

fileErrors.type: That file type isn't supported. Use PNG, JPG or WebP.
fileErrors.size: That image is larger than 8 MB.

spec.ok: Meets the sprite spec (32×32, hard edges, limited palette).
spec.empty: Almost empty: try turning off background removal

sprite.nothingFound: Couldn't find a character in this image. Try turning off “Remove plain background”.

editor.title: Pixel editor
editor.canvas: Sprite pixels, 32 by 32. Use the pointer to draw.
editor.note: Edits change the sprite. The portrait stays as it was.

warm: Oh, I don't mind telling you. “{text}”
teasing: “{text}” Don't laugh. Okay, you can laugh a little.
probing: Why do you want to know? ...“{text}” Your turn.
Before I answer, who's asking? ...All right. “{text}”
rambling: So, okay, long story, but basically: “{text}” ...and that's the short version!
“{text}” Wait, did I already tell you that? Anyway!
Oh! That reminds me: “{text}” Where was I?
formal: “{text}” I trust that answers your question.

happy: Something has put {name} in a good mood. {detail}
anxious: {name} looks like they're bracing for something. {detail}
irritated: {name}'s jaw is set. Best tread lightly. {detail}
excited: {name}'s eyes are bright with some new idea. {detail}
suspicious: {name} is watching everyone a little too carefully. {detail}
embarrassed: {name} is pretending very hard that nothing happened. {detail}

confide: {other} sits down next to {name}. “Can I tell you something? {text}”
Out of nowhere, {other} admits something to {name}: “{text}”
{other} lowers their voice. “{name}, I've never said this out loud. {text}”
argument: It starts small, then {other} tells {name} they're wrong about ‘{text}’.
{name} and {other} end up on opposite sides, and it's about ‘{text}’.
misunderstanding: {name} catches half a sentence from {other}: “...can't trust them...” Wait. Them who?
{name} sees {other} quickly hide a note. Probably nothing. Probably.
{other} laughs right as {name} walks in. Was that about {name}?
kindness: {other} quietly leaves something warm next to {name}.
{other} fixes the thing {name} was struggling with, without making a fuss.
{other} saves {name} the good seat in the {place}.
tease: {other} does a spot-on impression of {name}. Everyone saw.
“Oh no,” says {other}, “{name} has an idea again.”
askHelp: {name} needs a hand with this: ‘{text}’. {other} is right there.
{name} realizes they can't manage ‘{text}’ alone. They look at {other}.
A chance to get closer to ‘{text}’ appears, but it needs two people. {other} is nearby.
rivalry: {name} and {other} reach for the same thing in the {place} at the same moment.
Only one of them can win this. {name} and {other} both know it.
{other} gets the credit for something {name} did. Or did they?
rumor: Someone in the {place} whispers a rumor about {other}. {name} hears every word.
Word around the {place} is that {other} has been hiding something.
temptation: An easy shortcut appears, but it would mean going against this: ‘{text}’.
Someone offers {name} exactly what they want, if they bend ‘{text}’. Just once.
No one is watching. {name} could ignore ‘{text}’ and nobody would know.
goalStep: Something in the {place} might bring {name} closer to ‘{text}’.
A clue about ‘{text}’ turns up where {name} least expected it.
{name} gets a real chance to work on ‘{text}’.
fearTrigger: Something in the {place} brushes too close to {name}'s fear: ‘{text}’.
For a moment the {place} feels exactly like ‘{text}’. {name} goes still.
A small, ordinary thing reminds {name} of ‘{text}’.
memoryEcho: A smell, a sound, and {name} is back in {memory}.
quietMoment: A quiet moment. {name} does what they always do: ‘{text}’.
Nothing happens, and {name} slips into an old habit: ‘{text}’.
The {place} goes quiet. You notice something about {name}: ‘{text}’.

western-fantasy: A crow lands nearby and very clearly says “{name}”. Then it leaves.
Every candle in the {place} leans the same way for a moment.
A prophecy scroll blows past. The last line is smudged, as usual.
modern: Every phone in the {place} buzzes at once. Same message: “soon”.
The lights flicker, and a song nobody chose starts playing.
A delivery arrives addressed to {name}. Nobody ordered it.
ancient-china: A paper crane lands on {name}'s sleeve, carrying a sealed message.
A wandering swordsman bows to {name} as if they've met before.
The temple bell rings once, though no one is near it.
otherworld: Gravity takes a short break. Everything floats an inch, then settles.
A glowing plant in the {place} turns to follow {name}.
A small creature trades {name} a pebble for a button and runs off.

interior: {name} finds a note tucked under a loose floorboard.
Behind a cupboard, {name} finds a key that fits nothing here.
{name} finds a drawer that wasn't there yesterday.
street: {name} spots a dropped map with one street circled.
A stall {name} has never noticed is selling exactly one thing.
{name} finds a coin stamped with an unfamiliar face.
wilderness: {name} finds footprints that stop in the middle of a field.
Under a mossy stone, {name} finds a tiny carved door.
{name} finds a ribbon tied around a tree, very deliberately.
ruins: {name} uncovers a mural of someone who looks a lot like them.
{name} finds a lantern that's still warm.
A loose stone reveals a hollow with a sealed letter inside.
dreamscape: {name} finds a door standing on its own, slightly open.
{name} finds a clock with no hands, ticking anyway.
{name} finds a photograph of a day that hasn't happened yet.

progress: It works. A real step forward.
Against the odds, it pays off.
setback: It doesn't go to plan. Not even close.
A setback. Annoying, but not the end.

withdraw: ...I'm going to go stand over there.
Can we talk about this later, {other}?
comfort: That makes sense. Thank you for telling me.
You don't have to carry that alone, {other}.
joke: Well, that's going in my memoir.
If we survive this, I'm telling everyone.
investigate: Wait. What exactly do you mean, {other}?
Hm. Who else knows about this?
Something doesn't add up. Walk me through it.
act: Don't stop me. I've already decided.
cooperate: Okay, {other}. Let's figure it out together.
We're better at this as a team, {other}.

joke: Of course this happens to me.
Ten out of ten, very weird.
investigate: Hold on. Let me look closer.
There's a reason for this. I'll find it.
act: No time to think. Going for it!
I'll just... try it and see!
cooperate: I should tell the others about this.
This is a job for more than one person.

up: Something between {name} and {other} gets a little warmer.
{name} and {other} understand each other a bit better now.
down: Things between {name} and {other} get a little colder.
A small crack appears between {name} and {other}.
